e: Amplitude of accommodation declines c̅ age; ~+14D is typical around 7 years (Duane's curve).
Retrobulbar neuritis: painful ↓ vision c̅ RAPD and a normal disc (patient sees nothing, doctor sees nothing).
APACG: sudden pain, halos, mid-dilated fixed pupil, hazy cornea, ↑ IOP.
Ring infiltrate in a contact-lens wearer → Acanthamoeba keratitis; calcofluor white stains the cyst wall.
Krukenberg spindle (pigment on corneal endothelium) → pigmentary glaucoma.
ETDRS needs letter recognition – not for preverbal children (OKN drum, Teller, Cardiff cards are used).
Acute hydrops in keratoconus (Descemet break): intracameral gas (C₃F₈/SF₆) tamponade.
Frontal eye field (Brodmann area 8) controls voluntary scanning/saccades.
Acute haemorrhagic conjunctivitis: Enterovirus 70 and Coxsackie A24.
McCarey-Kaufman (MK) medium stores donor cornea; nylon (10-0) is the usual suture.
PDR: fibrovascular proliferation contracts → tractional retinal detachment.
NPCBVI blindness: presenting visual acuity <3/60 in the better eye.
Amblyopia is treated c̅ refractive correction, patching, penalisation, video games; strabismus surgery does not treat amblyopia.
OCT gives high-resolution cross-sectional imaging of all retinal layers.
Retrobulbar optic neuritis can have a normal disc (no disc oedema).
Excimer laser (193 nm) photoablates corneal stroma in LASIK/PRK.
Delayed post-cataract endophthalmitis (weeks) → Propionibacterium acnes (indolent, capsular plaque).
Orbit's sensory supply is from the trigeminal n. (ophthalmic and maxillary divisions).
